entities.summary: Jakob Wimpfeling was a German Renaissance humanist and theologian who played a pivotal role in the development of early modern Christian theology. Born in 1488, Wimpfeling was a prominent figure in the Reformation, and his works had a significant impact on the theological debates of his time. He was a key contributor to the 'Heidelberg Disputation,' a major theological controversy that took place in 1516, where he expressed his views on the nature of Christ and the authority of the Church. Wimpfeling's writings also influenced the development of Lutheranism and Calvinism, and he is considered one of the most important figures in the early Reformation. His legacy can be seen in the continued theological debates and conflicts that shaped the course of modern Christianity.
